st.3: Its ten-sign signboard was found near the South Gate.

st.2: Harappa lay on the Ravi; Lothal, not Harappa, was the port city.

st.4: Its Mound 7 cemetery has yielded 56 skeletons.

st.2: It is Ptolemy, not Pliny, who puts this drain at about 50 million sesterces a year.

st.3: It calls the Sabha and Samiti the twin daughters of Indra.
st.4: It forms part of the Trayi.

st.3: Thotlakonda and Bavikonda are hilltop monasteries of Visakhapatnam district.

st.3: The Digambaras hold that Mahavira never married.

x: All three statements are correct: Sthulabhadra's monks stayed in Magadha and wore white, the Digambaras hold that women must be reborn as men for moksha, and they hold that Mahavira never married (the Svetambaras say he married Yashoda).

st.3: The Schism edict, expelling dissenting monks and nuns, is found at Sarnath, Sanchi and Kaushambi.

st.1: Besnagar is known for the Heliodorus pillar, not for an Ashokan edict.

st.2: A bell-shaped inverted lotus sits between the shaft and the abacus.

st.2: Fa-hien came before Xuan Zang and I-Qing.
st.4: Harishena was his minister responsible for the Udayagiri conquests.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Stage 3 temples (Deogarh) had a low square shikhara, the beginning of the Nagara style.

st.2: Moksha is not part of the trivarga; it is the fourth purushartha.

x: All three statements are correct: dharma, artha and kama form the trivarga, moksha is the fourth purushartha outside it, and devotional Hinduism replaced sacrificial Brahmanism.

st.3: She made Balban Amir-i-Shikar.

st.1: His expeditions to Bengal against Haji Iliyas were successful.

st.3: Both were introduced by Alauddin Khalji.

st.2: Babur's army of about 12,000 faced about 1,00,000 troops of Daulat Khan Lodi.

st.1: Kandahar was lost to Shah Abbas I of Persia in 1622.

st.4: Nimbarka was born into a Tamil Brahmin family.

st.4: Vallabhacharya developed the views of Vishnuswami.

st.3: Sir Thomas Roe's mission secured a formal commercial treaty with Jahangir.
st.4: Edward Terry came to Jahangir's court as the chaplain of William Hawkins.

st.3: Ralph Fitch was the first Englishman to visit the court of Jahangir.

st.3: Forde captured Machilipatnam from the French in 1759.
st.4: Guntur passed to the English in 1788, before the other Northern Circars.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct; Forde took Machilipatnam in 1759. Statement 4 is wrong: Guntur came in 1788, after the other Circars (1765-68).

st.2: The big zamindars of Bengal joined the revolt.
st.4: Kadiri, where an attempt was made to incite rebellion in 1857, is in Coastal Andhra.

st.4: By the Treaty of Bassein the Peshwa gave up the chauth on the Nizam's territory.

st.3: Ranjit Singh died in June 1839.

st.1: Motilal Tejawat founded the Samp Sabha in 1883.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Govind Giri, not Motilal Tejawat, founded the Samp Sabha (1883).

st.3: The Girni Kamgar Union of Bombay was founded by S.A. Dange and the communists in 1928.

st.1: It did not hold the Vedas to be infallible.

st.1: The Tattvabodhini Patrika, organ of the Tattvabodhini Sabha, was published in English.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Tattvabodhini Patrika was published in Bengali.

st.2: He rejected the traditional philosophic systems of the East as worthless.

st.1: Karunalayam (1909), the only orphanage in Andhra, was founded by Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Karunalayam was founded by the Pithapuram Raja; Chilakamarti founded the Ram Mohan Roy School (1909).

st.1: He spread the Brahmo faith in Andhra and set up the Brahma Mandir at Kakinada.

x: Both statements are correct: Venkataratnam Naidu spread the Brahmo faith (Brahma Mandir, Kakinada), and he kept away from the national movement and the Theosophical Society.

st.3: The Deoband Movement was loyal to the British.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Aligarh was loyal to the British, while Deoband was anti-British.

st.2: Its first session demanded elected, not nominated, legislative councils.
st.4: It was from the start a mass body of the peasantry.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct; the first session asked for elected councils, not provincial autonomy. Statement 4 is wrong: the early Congress was an urban, English-educated middle-class body.

st.1: Faizpur (1936) was the first rural session of the Congress.
st.2: The National Planning Committee set up at the time of the Haripura session had Subhas Chandra Bose as its chairman.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct; Faizpur (1936), not Haripura, was the first rural session. Statement 2 is wrong: the National Planning Committee's chairman was Jawaharlal Nehru.

st.2: It was appointed in November 1927 by Ramsay MacDonald's Labour government.

st.2: Potti Sriramulu began his fast at Sambamurthy's house in Mylapore on 19 October 1952.

st.4: Naa Jeevita Yatra is the autobiography of Tanguturi Prakasam, not of Venkatappayya.

st.4: The SRC held that Hyderabad was unsuitable as a capital and a new capital would be needed.

st.3: Andhra Buddhism rejected the Pratitya Samutpada doctrine.

st.4: The ayakapatas of Amaravati show the Buddha in human form.

st.2: Errana wrote both the Harivamsamu and the Uttara Harivamsa.

st.4: Errana, who completed the rest of the Aranya Parva, was patronised by the Kakatiya ruler Prataparudra II.

st.1: The Kalamalla inscription (Kadapa), the first Telugu inscription, is dated to about 575 CE.
st.4: The Motupalli record is among the inscriptions showing written Telugu before Nannaya.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct; Kalamalla dates to c. 575 CE. Statement 4 is wrong: Motupalli is a later Kakatiya record, not a pre-Nannaya one.

st.2: The Vedic commentaries of Sayana and Madhava were begun on Bukka I's order and completed under Harihara II.

st.1: The Satrasala inscription is a record of the Palnadu Haihayas.

st.2: Niti Shastra Muktavali was written by Baddena.

st.2: It froze the allocation of seats on the basis of the 1971 Census, a freeze later ended by the 84th Amendment.
st.4: It added the word 'Justice' to the Preamble.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: 'armed rebellion' came with the 44th Amendment. Statement 2 is wrong: the 84th Amendment extended the 1971-Census freeze, not ended it. Statement 4 is wrong: it added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity'.

st.1: It extended SC/ST seat reservation under Article 335 up to 2030.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the seat reservation extended to 2030 is under Article 334, not 335.

st.3: The 131st Amendment Bill, 2026, raising the Lok Sabha ceiling to 850, was passed by the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 131st Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha on 17 April 2026.

st.2: It can vote on the Demands for Grants.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: only the Lok Sabha votes on the Demands for Grants.

st.3: Even a constitutional amendment under Article 368 cannot add a law to the Ninth Schedule.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: an Article 368 amendment can add laws to the Ninth Schedule; only the basic structure cannot be destroyed.

st.2: It gave blanket immunity to all Ninth Schedule laws.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Coelho held post-1973 Ninth Schedule laws open to review.

st.4: Both the Union Territories, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, have a legislature.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: J&K was created with a legislature, Ladakh without one.

st.2: Like the US Vice-President, he succeeds to the Presidency for the rest of the unexpired term when the President dies.
st.4: Under Article 79 he is a part of Parliament, along with the President and the two Houses.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: unlike the US VP, he only acts as President until a new one is elected. Statement 4 is wrong: Parliament is the President and the two Houses; the VP is not a part of it.

st.3: The 7th Amendment, 1956 provided a Council for Madhya Pradesh, and it functions today.
st.4: Tamil Nadu abolished its Council in 1969 and West Bengal in 1986.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: MP's Council was never created. Statement 4 is wrong: West Bengal abolished its Council in 1969 and Tamil Nadu in 1986.

st.2: Lakshadweep and Chandigarh have one Rajya Sabha seat each.
st.3: Its nominated members vote in the election of the President but not of the Vice-President.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: only Delhi, Puducherry and J&K have RS seats. Statement 3 is wrong: nominated members vote for the Vice-President but not the President.

st.2: The House must pass a resolution before such a seat falls vacant.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: under Article 101(3)(a) the seat falls vacant immediately, without any House resolution.

st.2: The Constitution provides for three sessions – Budget, Monsoon and Winter.
st.3: The Winter session is usually the longest session.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the three sessions are a convention, not in the Constitution. Statement 3 is wrong: the Budget session is the longest and the Winter the shortest.

st.2: The 1998 Act on Leaders and Chief Whips put the office of Whip into the Rules of Procedure.
st.4: A three-line whip merely informs members of a vote and leaves them free to abstain.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1998 Act only gives facilities. Statement 4 is wrong: a three-line whip directs members to vote strictly as the party directs; a one-line whip merely informs.

st.4: The Governor of Andhra Pradesh can still nominate one Anglo-Indian member to the Assembly.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Anglo-Indian nomination ended with the 104th Amendment from 25 January 2020.

All three statements are correct: Sanjiva Reddy, from Anantapur and AP's first CM, was the only President elected unopposed; Pranab Mukherjee dropped 'His Excellency' in 2012; and Rajendra Prasad alone was elected twice.

st.2: His office, governed by the Law Officers (Terms and Conditions) Rules, 1987, is filled on the advice of the Union Public Service Commission.
st.3: Like the Attorney General, he has the right to take part in the proceedings of Parliament under Article 88.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the SG is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (normal term 3 years). Statement 3 is wrong: the SG has no Article 88 right; only the AG has it.

st.2: The right to receive immediate information of the arrest of a member is an individual privilege of that member.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the right to immediate information of a member's arrest is a collective privilege of the House.
Both statements are correct: judicial review asks whether the law is valid, and judicial activism asks whether it is just.

st.2: It hears second civil appeals on any question of fact or law.
st.3: Only the Calcutta, Bombay and Madras High Courts have original civil jurisdiction in high-value cases.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: second appeals lie only on a substantial question of law. Statement 3 is wrong: four HCs, including Delhi, have original civil jurisdiction.

st.3: Like the USA, Canada vests residuary powers in its provinces.
st.4: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, residuary powers were vested in the Federal Legislature.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Canada vests residuary powers in the Centre, unlike the USA. Statement 4 is wrong: the 1935 Act vested them in the Governor-General.

st.2: The Union assumes full legislative and executive control only during a Financial Emergency.
st.3: A National Emergency can be declared only for the whole of India and not for a part of it.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: full Union control comes only with a National Emergency. Statement 3 is wrong: since the 42nd Amendment a National Emergency may cover any part of India.

st.2: According to Dr Ambedkar, the States have a limited right to secede with the consent of Parliament.
st.4: Like the USA, India is an indestructible Union of indestructible States.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Ambedkar said the States have no right to secede. Statement 4 is wrong: India is an indestructible Union of destructible States.

st.3: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse (Articles 301-307) is a Fundamental Right in Part III of the Constitution.
st.4: Under Article 255, an Act is invalid for want of the required previous sanction even if assent was later given.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Articles 301-307 are in Part XIII, not a Fundamental Right. Statement 4 is wrong: under Article 255 later assent cures the lack of previous sanction.

st.3: The Lokpal Act, 2013 replaced the DSPE Act as the law governing the CBI.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the CBI still works under the DSPE Act, 1946; the Second ARC (2007) recommended a new law to replace it.

st.1: The AP SIC's website sic.ap.gov.in was launched on 8 September 2025, before the High Court's direction on an online RTI portal.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the SIC website came on 8 September 2025, after the High Court's direction of November 2023.

st.1: Under Article 356, the Union may give directions to a State on any matter.
st.2: Under Article 353, the State governments are suspended.
st.4: The term of the Lok Sabha can be extended by the President by one year at a time.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: directions on any matter come under Article 353. Statement 2 is wrong: State governments are not suspended. Statement 4 is wrong: the extension, one year at a time, is made by Parliament by law.

st.2: SCS was granted by the Finance Commission, which funded 90% of the State's plan assistance.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: SCS was granted by the NDC on Planning Commission advice; the Centre funded 90% of plan assistance.

st.1: The Planning Commission, replaced by NITI Aayog, was a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Planning Commission was set up by a Cabinet resolution and was non-statutory.

st.3: Its chairman, Dr P.V. Rajamannar, was a former Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court.
st.4: Besides the chairman, its members were A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar and C.N. Annadurai.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Rajamannar was a former Chief Justice of the Madras High Court. Statement 4 is wrong: the other members were A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar and P. Chandra Reddy.
Both statements are correct: regional parties can improve the representation of backward regions, but may also encourage parochialism and instability.

st.1: In coalition politics they have never supplied a Lok Sabha Speaker.
st.3: The Trinamool Congress defeated the BJP in West Bengal in 2026.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: regional parties have acted as kingmakers, supplying Speakers and Union Ministers. Statement 3 is wrong: the BJP defeated the Trinamool in West Bengal in 2026.

st.1: Andhra Pradesh has 4 SC-reserved Lok Sabha seats, including Nellore, and 1 ST-reserved seat.
st.3: Telangana's ST-reserved Lok Sabha seats are Adilabad and Nagarkurnool.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AP's SC seats are Amalapuram, Bapatla, Chittoor and Tirupati; Nellore is general. Statement 3 is wrong: Telangana's ST seats are Adilabad and Mahabubabad; Nagarkurnool is SC.

st.2: Under Section 8(4), a convicted sitting MP who appeals within three months is not disqualified.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Section 8(4) was struck down in Lily Thomas (2013); conviction with 2+ years' jail disqualifies at once.

st.3: The Committee recommended holding local-body polls on the same day as the Lok Sabha and Assembly polls.
st.4: The British constructive vote of no-confidence was suggested as a safeguard.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: local-body polls were to follow within 100 days. Statement 4 is wrong: the safeguard idea was the German constructive vote of no-confidence.

st.2: It continued revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 16th FC dropped revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants.

st.2: Public order is an item of the Eleventh Schedule.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: public order is not in the Eleventh Schedule (it is a State List subject).

st.1: The provisions on minor minerals and minor forest produce are among the best implemented.
st.3: Odisha had notified its final PESA rules by April 2026.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: minor-mineral and MFP provisions are the least implemented. Statement 3 is wrong: Odisha had only draft rules in April 2026.

st.1: The proviso to Article 164(1) requires a Minister for tribal welfare in Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha.
st.3: After the first notification under Article 342, the Governor may include or exclude communities from the ST list by public notification.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 94th Amendment (2006) replaced Bihar with Chhattisgarh. Statement 3 is wrong: later changes to the ST list can be made only by Parliament by law.

st.1: It is constituted every five years by the State Election Commission.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the SFC is constituted by the Governor, not the State Election Commission.
Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: PESA extends Part IX to the Fifth Schedule areas, not the Sixth Schedule areas.

st.3: It was proposed by the Narasimham Committee (1991).
st.4: Fixing the repo rate is one of its roles.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the FSDC was proposed by the Raghuram Rajan Committee (2008). Statement 4 is wrong: fixing the repo rate is not its role (that is the MPC's).

st.2: These Upper-Layer NBFCs must get listed within 3 years, as directed by SEBI.
st.3: The Indian Financial System Code has 11 characters, the first four of which are the branch code.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 3-year listing rule is the RBI's. Statement 3 is wrong: the first four letters are the bank code; the last six are the branch code.

st.1: It involves the permanent sale of public assets.
st.4: The National Monetisation Pipeline covers both greenfield and brownfield assets.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: monetisation is not a sale; rights are leased for a limited period. Statement 4 is wrong: the NMP covers brownfield assets only.

st.1: Its implementing ministry is the Ministry of Communications.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Digital India is implemented by the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY).

st.1: The 2016 retrospective amendment followed a 2014 ruling of the Supreme Court.
st.2: The 2020 amendment raised the ceiling on administrative expenses from 20% to 50%.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 2016 amendment followed a 2014 Delhi High Court ruling. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2020 amendment cut the cap from 50% to 20%.

st.4: Of the 99 AIBP priority projects funded through NABARD's LTIF, 8 are in Andhra Pradesh.

x: All four statements are correct: minor projects have a CCA up to 2,000 ha, major ones above 10,000 ha, minor irrigation gives about 65% of irrigated area, and 8 of the 99 AIBP priority projects are in AP.

st.2: Jonnagiri, India's first private gold mine, is located in Kurnool district.

x: All three statements are correct: beach-sand minerals occur on the Srikakulam–Kakinada coast, Jonnagiri (first private gold mine) is in Kurnool, and bauxite occurs at Araku, Chintapalli and Paderu.

st.3: The 2011 population of 495.77 lakh refers to the residual (13-district) Andhra Pradesh.

x: All three statements are correct for the residual State: AP ranked 10th with 4.09% of India's population, and 495.77 lakh is the residual AP figure (undivided AP had about 7%).

All three statements are correct: India's population was 121.09 crore with 17.7% decadal growth, the rural share was 68.9%, and it was the 15th national Census with the motto 'Our Census, Our Future'.

st.2: Antyodaya first started in Gujarat in 1977-78.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Antyodaya first started in Rajasthan (1977-78).

st.2: The 2004-05 figure came from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS).

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2004-05 figure came from the NSS 61st round; the PLFS began only in 2017-18.

st.3: The sample was reduced to about half of its earlier size.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the sample was raised, to about 2,72,304 households.

st.2: Since 2010 the HDI is the arithmetic mean of the three dimension indices.
st.4: India's HDI of 0.685 in HDR 2025 places it in the 'High' category.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: since 2010 the HDI is the geometric mean. Statement 4 is wrong: 0.685 is in the 'Medium' category, just below 0.700.

st.2: The leading process of land degradation is vegetation degradation, followed by water erosion.
st.3: Desertification declined in 28 of 31 States/UTs.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: water erosion leads (10.98%), then vegetation degradation. Statement 3 is wrong: desertification rose in 28 of 31 States/UTs.

st.2: As per the UNDP's Global MPI, 24.82 crore people exited multidimensional poverty in nine years.
st.4: Andhra Pradesh's MPI value rose from 0.025 to 0.053.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 24.82 crore figure is from NITI Aayog's discussion paper. Statement 4 is wrong: AP's MPI fell from 0.053 to 0.025.

st.1: Max O. Lorenz introduced the Lorenz curve in 1905 to show the link between growth and environmental degradation.
st.3: Arthur Laffer put forward the inverted-U hypothesis linking inequality and income in 1955.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Lorenz curve (1905) shows income distribution; the growth–environment curve is the Environmental Kuznets curve. Statement 3 is wrong: the inverted-U hypothesis (1955) is Simon Kuznets's.

st.2: The 45° diagonal line shows perfect inequality.
st.3: The farther the curve bows away from the 45° line, the lower the inequality.
st.4: It gives a single numerical measure of inequality.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 45° line shows perfect equality. Statement 3 is wrong: the farther the bow, the greater the inequality. Statement 4 is wrong: the curve is a graph; the Gini coefficient gives the number.

st.2: After the Planning Commission was wound up, central funds are allocated to the States by NITI Aayog.
st.3: NITI Aayog decides the method and formula for sharing tax proceeds between the Centre and the States.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: central funds are now allocated by the Union Finance Ministry. Statement 3 is wrong: the sharing formula is decided by the Finance Commission.

st.2: The steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur and Bokaro were set up during it.
st.3: Chittaranjan made railway coaches and Perambur made locomotives.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Second Plan's steel plants were Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela (Bokaro came later). Statement 3 is wrong: Chittaranjan made locomotives and Perambur coaches.

st.2: India's current account deficit peaked at 4.8% of GDP in FY 2008-09.
st.3: An Economic Stabilisation Fund of ₹57,381 crore was set up after oil fell below $50 per barrel in March 2026.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the CAD peaked at about 4.8% of GDP in 2012-13, not 2008-09. Statement 3 is wrong: the fund followed the $100 per barrel oil shock of March 2026.

st.1: Corporation tax is a Union tax kept outside the shared pool.
st.2: Agricultural income tax is a Union tax.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: since the 80th Amendment (2000) corporation tax is in the shared pool. Statement 2 is wrong: agricultural income tax is a State tax.

st.1: It was constituted on 27 November 2017 under Article 263.
st.2: It was chaired by Dr Y.V. Reddy.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Finance Commissions are constituted under Article 280. Statement 2 is wrong: the 15th FC was chaired by N.K. Singh (Y.V. Reddy chaired the 14th).

st.2: Population (1971) carries a weight of 17.5%.
st.4: The tax effort criterion has been retained with a weight of 2.5%.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 17.5% weight is for the 2011 population. Statement 4 is wrong: the tax effort criterion was dropped.

st.1: Audited accounts need be placed in the public domain only by urban local bodies, not by rural ones.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: at least 25% of rural local bodies must place provisional and audited accounts online.

st.1: Under the RBI framework of March 2022, a microfinance loan is a loan backed by collateral to a household with annual income up to ₹3 lakh.
st.2: Under the same framework, the 50% cap on a household's repayments applies only to NBFC-MFIs, not to banks.
st.4: Women make up only a minority of microfinance borrowers in India.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: a microfinance loan is collateral-free. Statement 2 is wrong: the 50% cap applies to all regulated lenders. Statement 4 is wrong: about 95% of borrowers are women.

st.2: IFCI was the last of the three to be set up.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: IFCI (1948) was the first, followed by ICICI (1955) and IDBI (1964).

st.2: In Budget 2026-27 the revenue deficit is larger than the fiscal deficit.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the fiscal deficit (4.3%) is far larger than the revenue deficit (1.5%).

st.1: The distribution function provides public goods such as the judiciary and a lighthouse.
st.2: Education is a pure public good.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: providing public goods is the allocation function. Statement 2 is wrong: education is a merit good, not a pure public good.

st.1: It applies to all companies regardless of size.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Pillar Two applies only to large multinational groups (revenue of €750 million or more).

st.1: The word 'budget' comes from the French 'bougette' (little bag), and Article 112 of the Constitution uses the word 'budget'.
st.4: As the main instrument of monetary policy, the Budget performs allocation, redistribution and stabilisation functions.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Constitution does not use the word 'budget'; Article 112 speaks of the Annual Financial Statement. Statement 4 is wrong: the Budget is the main instrument of fiscal policy.

st.1: It replaced the MEIS, which had been upheld by the WTO.
st.3: It is run online by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the MEIS was challenged and ruled against at the WTO. Statement 3 is wrong: RoDTEP is run online by the CBIC.

st.2: By 2025, action plans had been prepared for more districts than had export products identified.
st.3: Srikakulam is one of Andhra Pradesh's priority districts in the 90-day campaign from 1 June 2026.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: products were identified in 734 districts, action plans prepared for 590. Statement 3 is wrong: Srikakulam is not among AP's priority districts.

st.1: It is an expenditure-reducing policy, making domestic goods cheaper for foreigners and imports costlier at home.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: devaluation is an expenditure-switching policy. Statement 2 is wrong: devaluation lowers the foreign-currency prices of exports.

st.2: Only the Allied great powers – the USA, the UK, the USSR and China – took part in it.
st.4: The IMF was formally created on 27 December 1945, India joining it only after independence.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 44 nations took part. Statement 4 is wrong: India was a founding member of the IMF on 27 December 1945.

st.1: The India-EU TEPA came into force on 1 October 2025.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the TEPA in force from 1 October 2025 is with EFTA, not the EU.

st.3: Kalyan Sona and Sonalika are Indian selections from IRRI's dwarf rice.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Kalyan Sona and Sonalika are wheats selected from Borlaug's Mexican dwarf wheats.

st.2: Land ceiling is the legally stipulated minimum size of holding an individual or family must hold.
st.3: Tenancy reforms largely succeeded, with hardly any 'voluntary surrenders' or evictions.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a land ceiling is the legal maximum holding. Statement 3 is wrong: tenancy reforms largely failed through 'voluntary surrenders' and evictions.

st.2: The PLPs roll up into the Lead Bank's District Credit Plan, which is the final State document.
st.3: The State Focus Paper is prepared by the RBI.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the PLPs roll up into the State Focus Paper. Statement 3 is wrong: the State Focus Paper is NABARD's.

st.1: MSP is announced for 22 mandated crops, and sugarcane gets a Statutory Minimum Price.
st.3: Raw jute is not covered under MSP.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: sugarcane gets the FRP, which replaced the SMP from 2009-10. Statement 3 is wrong: raw jute is covered, as a commercial crop.

st.1: Automatic approval up to 51% foreign equity applied to all industries.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: automatic approval up to 51% applied only to listed high-priority industries.

st.3: In WHR 2026 India was 116th and Denmark topped the list.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India was 116th, but Finland topped the list for the ninth year running.

st.1: Bank and financial institution funds are freed for productive use.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: industrial sickness turns bank and FI funds into NPAs rather than freeing them.

st.1: Kerala gets 64.3% of its GSVA from services, while Bihar gets most of its GSVA from agriculture.
st.3: In 2023-24 (NITI Aayog) Delhi had the highest services share in State GDP, at 88.8%.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Bihar too gets 58.7% of its GSVA from services. Statement 3 is wrong: Chandigarh led at 88.8% (Delhi 84.1%).

st.1: The National Industrial Classification (NIC) is prepared by the WTO.
st.3: Health and real estate services are placed in the Union List.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NIC is India's own classification (MoSPI), listing 15 types of services; the WTO uses the UNCPC. Statement 3 is wrong: health and real estate are State List subjects.

st.3: STPI, India's first export-park model for software, was set up under the Ministry of Commerce.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: STPI (1991) was set up under the Department of Electronics.

st.1: SES 2025-26 is presented by the Union Ministry of Finance.
st.2: The last chapter of SES 2025-26 is 'Progress Monitoring – KPIs and SDGs'.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the SES is the Andhra Pradesh Government's survey (it has 11 chapters). Statement 2 is wrong: that was SES 2024-25's last chapter; SES 2025-26 ends with 'Data-Driven Governance'.

st.4: The 16th Finance Commission recommended keeping them outside the budget.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the 16th FC recommended bringing off-budget borrowings on budget.

st.1: Section 90(3) requires the express consent of Telangana.
st.2: Under Section 90(4) the Government of Andhra Pradesh obtains the environmental, forest and R&R clearances.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Section 90(3) deems Telangana's consent to have been given. Statement 2 is wrong: under 90(4) the Central Government executes the project and obtains the clearances.

st.2: Seventh Schedule funds under Section 52, including the Calamity Relief Fund, were divided by population ratio.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Section 52 funds went by population, but the Calamity Relief Fund was divided by area.

st.2: Its Rayalaseema districts are Anantapur, Kurnool, YSR Kadapa and Nellore.
st.3: It was modelled on the Special Category Status given to the north-eastern States.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the fourth Rayalaseema district is Chittoor, not Nellore. Statement 3 is wrong: the package was modelled on the KBK and Bundelkhand packages.

st.2: AP kept short-term and long-term cooperative credit in separate structures.
st.3: Primary agricultural development banks were retained alongside PACS under the Single Window system.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: AP integrated short- and long-term credit from 1986. Statement 3 is wrong: primary agricultural development banks were abolished in 1987.

st.1: The Prakasam Barrage at Vijayawada replaced the 1850s anicut of K.L. Rao.
st.3: Nagarjuna Sagar is one of the largest earthen dams.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the barrage (begun 1954) replaced Sir Arthur Cotton's anicut. Statement 3 is wrong: Nagarjuna Sagar is one of the largest masonry dams.

st.1: NICDC, formerly the DMIC Development Corporation, works under NITI Aayog.
st.2: The Bharatmala Pariyojana proposed 14 Coastal Economic Zones.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: NICDC works under DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Statement 2 is wrong: the 14 CEZs were proposed by the Sagarmala National Perspective Plan (2016).

st.3: It was issued by the Union Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: it was issued by the AP Government (G.O.Ms. No. 11, Industries & Commerce, 2016); it aimed to train 1 lakh youth.
Both statements are correct: Stand-Up India covers greenfield enterprises only, and each bank branch should have at least one SC/ST and one woman borrower.

st.3: The AP Pumped Storage Power Promotion Policy 2022 was issued by the Union Ministry of Power.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: it is the AP Government's own policy, seeking to harness 33 GW of pumped storage.

st.1: Besides the Chairman, it has two members nominated by the RBI.
st.3: Of its five other members, all must be part-time members.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the two are from the Finance and Law ministries; only one member comes from the RBI. Statement 3 is wrong: at least three of the five must be whole-time members.

st.3: Its VELC payload made the first visible-light spectroscopy of coronal mass ejections.

x: All three statements are correct: Aditya-L1 was launched by PSLV-C57 from Sriharikota in 2023, it is in a halo orbit at L1 about 1.5 million km away, and VELC made the first visible-light spectroscopy of CMEs.

st.2: Titan is the largest moon of Saturn.

x: All four statements are correct: Ganymede is the largest moon and bigger than Mercury, Titan is Saturn's largest (Rhea second), Europa has a sub-surface ocean, and Titan has methane lakes about 100 m deep.

st.2: It is longer than the solar day.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the sidereal day is about 4 minutes shorter than the solar day.

st.2: It is maintained by the conservation of the Earth's angular momentum (gyroscopic effect).

x: All three statements are correct: the axis keeps pointing to the Pole Star, its parallelism is kept by conservation of angular momentum, and it gives opposite seasons in the two hemispheres.

st.3: Each earthquake has its own shadow zone, set by its epicentre.
